p1c1.caption: Figure I · The horizon tears
p1c1.opener_composition: Painted night star-map fills the slot; a horizontal canvas tear at the lower third reveals broadsheet columns beneath. Folio line above title; title left on desktop.
p1c1.opener_rationale: The title image is literal (ch ends: 'our boat has crashed into it, and left a big rip'). Painted — not engraved — per medium lock, so the tear reads as ruptured scenery, and the columns beneath preview the book's printed-serial identity.
p1c1.palette_role: gilt-dominant: gilt star-lines and map furniture on Night Ink; tear edges Newsprint.
p1c1.title: A Horizon Made of Canvas

p1c10.caption: Figure X · The Republic's balance-sheet, balanced
p1c10.opener_composition: Engraved double-entry ledger spread: the Republic's assets left, the Receiver's warrant right, gilt balance-rule struck across. Folio ledger band (No. X / ENTERED MMVIII) from Direction 3.
p1c10.opener_rationale: The chapter is a bankruptcy procedure — a balance-sheet is its native document. Tudor-engraved ledger keeps the ONE-engraving-cohort discipline while delivering the registry-ledger idea.
p1c10.palette_role: ledger vellum + gilt on oxblood-shadowed ground.
p1c10.title: A Simple Sovereign Bankruptcy Procedure

p1c11.caption: Figure XI · The diptych, posted
p1c11.opener_composition: Two red-ink posted bills side by side (LEFT / RIGHT) sharing one gilt frame; a Q-virus wax seal bridges the gutter. Blackletter bill heads are HTML overlays.
p1c11.opener_rationale: The chapter dissolves left-vs-right into organization theory — a diptych that is visibly one sheet makes the argument graphically. Red-ink proclamation craft per lock.
p1c11.palette_role: Signal Red bills on Press Black, gilt shared frame.
p1c11.title: The Truth About Left and Right

p1c12.caption: Figure XII · Against the dam
p1c12.opener_composition: Proclamation broadside: a ruled dam wall (Boulder Dam analogy, 'La Wik direct action') holding back a red-ink torrent of posted bills. Portrait-leaning composition, wall left, torrent right.
p1c12.opener_rationale: Ch 12's central set-piece is the Boulder Dam / direct-action analogy and the survey of tactics — dam-vs-torrent stages 'what is to be done' as pressure against a wall.
p1c12.palette_role: ink + Signal Red torrent, gilt wall rules.
p1c12.title: What Is to Be Done?

p1c13.caption: Figure XIII · Patent of the pilots
p1c13.opener_composition: Red-ink letters-patent: the pilots' directorate key large at center, Trust seal below, Plaincorp/Trust/Receiver hierarchy as a chancery table. Most formal opener in the book.
p1c13.opener_rationale: The chapter is a constitutional document (Trust, Receiver, PHT franchise) — letters-patent is its native form. Key + Trust knot carry the 'all power to the pilots' close.
p1c13.palette_role: brass + Signal Red seals on Press Black; closing cockade nearby in end-mark family.
p1c13.title: Tactics and Structures of Any Prospective Restoration

p1c14.caption: Figure XIV · Commissioned, dismissed, sealed
p1c14.opener_composition: Red-ink commission scroll unfurling over a small ember starfield; the white cockade returns as the closing seal. Mirror of ch 1's tear: the book opens by ripping scenery and closes by signing orders.
p1c14.opener_rationale: The send-off chapter (space-lieutenant framing, 'rules', the Bazaar/Cathedral close) wants ceremony: a commission, not an essay header. The closing cockade rhymes cover + ch 3 + ch 13.
p1c14.palette_role: ember starfield + Signal Red scroll + white cockade on near-black.
p1c14.title: Rules for Reactionaries

p1c2.caption: Figure II · The cabinet of anomalies
p1c2.opener_composition: Painted curiosity cabinet: tilted specimen frames (Kenya clip, Borboni, 1914 encirclement) pinned at angles over a torn wall-chart. Frames overlap; one pin is Signal Red.
p1c2.opener_rationale: The chapter is a specimen tray of historical anomalies that refuse to fit — tilted painted frames stage 'does not fit the chart' without a single engraved line.
p1c2.palette_role: gilt frames + Dim Type labels on painted umber ground; one signal pin.
p1c2.title: More Historical Anomalies

p1c3.caption: Figure III · For the King over the water
p1c3.opener_composition: The white Jacobite cockade large at center over painted Stuart-rose wallpaper; a torn corner reveals the progressive timeline beneath, already cracking.
p1c3.opener_rationale: The Jacobite chapter earns the book's own seal at full size: the cockade IS the chapter's argument (restoration as loyalty, not theory). Painted ground keeps the cohort medium pure.
p1c3.palette_role: white + gilt on painted rose-oxblood ground.
p1c3.title: The Jacobite History of the World

p1c4.caption: Figure IV · The first Whig
p1c4.opener_composition: Torn painted broadsheet of the Putney Debates nailed to a dark board; a small devil-tail fleuron tails the colophon. Salutation treatment debuts here (first 'dear open-minded progressive').
p1c4.opener_rationale: Dr. Johnson's quip ('the first Whig was the Devil') stages as a period sheet — Putney, the Dartmouth, the Tennis Court Oath are the chapter's named scenes. The tear continues the cohort grammar.
p1c4.palette_role: oxblood ink on painted newsprint scrap; gilt nail-heads.
p1c4.title: Dr. Johnson's Hypothesis

p1c5.caption: Figure V · Soundings for world peace
p1c5.opener_composition: Surveyor's blueprint: meridian lines, sounding marks, and treaty-column soundings charting the Stross letter's one-sentence plan. Widest plate in the cohort (longest chapter, 16.9k words).
p1c5.opener_rationale: The chapter is a navigational proposal (recognize every sovereignty; classical international law) — a survey chart is its native document, and blueprint craft keeps it technical, not romantic.
p1c5.palette_role: white-line on deep Chart-sea ground; gilt meridian ticks.
p1c5.title: The Shortest Way to World Peace

p1c6.caption: Figure VI · The clean room
p1c6.opener_composition: White-line schematic on Chart-sea: key-exchange diagram (Steve/Marc controller keys), circuit traces, responsibility grid. Most diagrammatic opener in the book — the mechanism laid bare.
p1c6.opener_rationale: 'Solving the problem from scratch' with cryptographic keys and controllers is literally a circuit diagram. Blueprint medium per lock; the key-tooth end-seal rhymes the key ceremony.
p1c6.title: The Lost Theory of Government

p1c7.caption: Figure VII · Specimen: the Beltway crater
p1c7.opener_composition: Specimen cyanotype: the teleported-Beltway crater rendered as a surveyed impact ring with dependency-diagram annotations in white line. Clinical, deadpan.
p1c7.opener_rationale: The Beltway-crater thought experiment is the chapter's signature image; cyanotype treatment keeps it evidentiary (a specimen, not a scene) inside the blueprint cohort.
p1c7.palette_role: cyanotype blue-white on Chart-sea; ash annotation ticks.
p1c7.title: The Ugly Truth About Government

p1c8.caption: Figure VIII · Warrant for a reset
p1c8.opener_composition: Engraved NRA-eagle warrant (the chapter names the eagle) beside a reset-vs-revolution diptych: apoptosis (clean seal-cut) vs. necrosis (ragged tear).
p1c8.opener_rationale: The chapter's hinge is reset≠revolution, apoptosis≠necrosis — a diptych makes the distinction structural, and the named eagle warrants the engraving craft.
p1c8.palette_role: gilt eagle on ink; oxblood seal-cut line.
p1c8.title: A Reset Is Not a Revolution

p1c9.caption: Figure IX · Inventory of a dissolution
p1c9.opener_composition: FLAGSHIP (520px): the engraved facade mid-dissolution — tracery unmasoned course by course, warrants and seals inventoried in the margins, guilloche ledger bands. The book's central metaphor at full ambition.
p1c9.opener_rationale: The signature chapter: 'uninstall a Cathedral' via the dissolution-of-the-monasteries precedent the text names. Tudor-inventory engraving is textually licensed here and nowhere else — hence the flagship scale and the medium lock.
p1c9.palette_role: oxblood-dominant: most saturated plate in the book; gilt warrants; ink shadows.
p1c9.title: How to Uninstall a Cathedral
